messages:
Alex: Hey team, ran an nsys capture of a 1k-batch RAG workload and the NVTX ranges look... noisy. Uploaded qdrep to /perf-artifacts/171905/ if you want the raw trace.
Maya: I pulled the timeline. There's a huge number of tiny NVTX push/pop pairs in the kernel selection and mid-loop code paths. Did you capture with nvtx tracing enabled?
Alex: Yep: `nsys profile --output=perf/171905 --trace=cuda,cudnn,nvtx --capture-range=nvtx --sample=none --force ./redwood-server --cfg perf/1k-rag.json`
perf-bot: nsys job 171905 completed. Artifacts: /perf-artifacts/171905/ (qdrep, timeline, flamegraph)
Sam: Those micro-ranges might explain the sim overhead we saw on tail latencies. NVTX pushes/pops aren't free, especially at 1-token latencies.
Jordan: Can we quantify the hit?
Alex: From this run:
- baseline (NVTX disabled) p50=41.9ms, p99=85.7ms
- current main (full NVTX) p50=43.0ms, p99=89.8ms
So about +2.6% p50 and +4.8% p99. For tiny batches (<8) p99 overhead reached ~7%.
Maya: Besides overhead, the timeline is unreadable: thousands of short string ranges hide kernel names. Makes root-cause hunting painful.
Priya: Another problem: our range strings include the full request UUID in several places, and our log aggregator now leaks long raw IDs into trace viewers. We should never put full PII or full UUIDs into NVTX range names.
Sam: Proposed guidelines to discuss:
1) Coarse-grained ranges for major phases only: `selector`, `kv_lookup`, `batching`, `compute_forward`, `kv_insert`.
2) Avoid per-layer per-op push/pop inside hot loops; use aggregate ranges plus cheap markers.
3) If request linkage is needed, push a single short per-request tag at request start using an 8-char truncated id.
Maya: For naming, propose ASCII-only, compact tokens: `<area>:<op>:<req8>` e.g. `selector:choose:af3e12b4`. Max length 64. No raw prompt text or full ids.
Jordan: Also add numeric payloads via nvtxRangePushEx so tooling can join traces by int key instead of parsing strings.
Alex: Example pseudo-code for C++ runtime: \n```\n// short per-request tag\nchar name[64];\nsnprintf(name, sizeof(name), "svc:%s:%s", area, short_req);\nnvtxRangePushA(name);\n// push a numeric payload in parallel\nnvtxEventAttributes_t attr = {0};\nattr.version = NVTX_VERSION;\nattr.size = NVTX_EVENT_ATTRIB_STRUCT_SIZE;\nattr.payload.type = NVTX_PAYLOAD_TYPE_UNSIGNED_INT64;\nattr.payload.u64 = (uint64_t)request_hash;\nnvtxRangePushEx(&attr);\n```\nSam: Numeric payloads are great for automated analysis. But note: nvtxRangePushEx behavior varies by driver; we should test on oldest GPUs in our fleet.
Priya: Agree. Also measure overhead: name-only vs name+ex vs no-nvtx. Driver quirks might add cost.
Alex: I ran a small matrix:
- no-nvtx: baseline
- name-only: +2.1% median
- name+ex: +2.6% median
So Ex adds a small delta but gives big observability gains.
Maya: Another trick: collapse many micro push/pops by pushing a composite range around the hot loop (e.g. `compute_forward:batch`) and emit `nvtxMarkA` for cheap markers inside. Marks show up in timeline but don't create nested ranges.
Jordan: Good idea. Markers are lighter than push/pop and still let us see micro-events without massive range churn.
Sam: For kernel selector specifically, let's only emit ranges for slow/rare paths. For the fast path (most requests), avoid ranges. We can gate with `if (selector_time > Xms || debug_nvtx) push_range()`.
Alex: I instrumented selector with a threshold and a debug flag; that reduced total range count by ~80% on a typical 1k trace.
Priya: Timeline also showed `kv_lookup` ranges overlapping GPU memcpy operations. We should separately annotate `memcpy:host2dev` / `memcpy:dev2host` and `kv:lookup` so it's clear which stalls are I/O vs compute.
Maya: Agreed. Proposed canonical range names: `kv:lookup`, `memcpy:h2d`, `memcpy:d2h`, `compute:kernel:<req8>`.
Alex: I also noticed a regression in selector after we swapped in a quantized kernel variant. Kernel timelines show many tiny grid launches. Might be our heuristics picking the wrong kernel for seq_len=32 vs 512.
Sam: I'll file a selector heuristics PR to prefer fused kernels when seq_len < 64 and small batch sizes; add a feature flag `selector_new_heuristics` so we can roll back if needed.
Jordan: I'll validate nvtxRangePushEx on A100 and RTX testbeds to ensure no driver regressions.
Maya: For post-processing, let's add a CSV exporter from qdrep that flattens ranges to rows: start_ns,end_ns,duration_ns,range_name,req_short,thread_id,kernel_name. That makes diffs and automated annotations easier. I'll prototype with the nsys Python bindings.
Sam: Also, we should add small unit tests that ensure range names conform to the ASCII/length/no-pii rules. Static checker in CI to enforce.
Priya: And normalize UTF-8 for all names. Non-ASCII chars break some viewers.
Alex: Action items I can own:
- PR: implement naming convention + numeric payload push (name+ex).
- PR: nvtx feature flag to reduce instrumentation in hot paths.
- Run overhead matrix (no-nvtx, name-only, name+ex) on batch sizes 1k/64/1 and post numbers.
Sam: I'll land the selector heuristics PR and add regression unit tests for kernel-choice boundaries.
Maya: I'll implement CSV post-processor and drop a sample mapping script.
Jordan: I'll run driver-level validation on old machines and report any nvtxRangePushEx anomalies.
perf-bot: Scheduled perf runs: 171905-nvtx-off, 171906-name-only, 171907-name+ex. Results will post here when complete.
Alex: Thanks everyone. Goal: readable timelines, safe names, and <3% median overhead keeping p99 regressions minimized. Raw qdrep is at /perf-artifacts/171905/ if you want to dig in.
